cases.summary_text: Hugging Face trained sparse autoencoders with 262 k features on the residual stream of layer 20 in Gemma‑2‑9B, uncovering monosemantic decoder directions such as “legal terminology,” “code error messages,” and “refusal to answer.” Activation‑patching experiments show that ablating the “refusal” direction reduces the model’s refusal rate on harmful prompts by 42 %, providing a causal link between a single interpretable feature and safety behavior. The SAE weights and a browser‑based visualizer are released, enabling researchers to explore and validate interpretable features in large language models.

cases.summary_text: Yohei Nakajima, the creator of BabyAGI, explained that the system uses a simple while‑loop with an LLM to decompose a goal into subtasks, execute them, and generate new tasks. The original design often caused agents to loop indefinitely and waste tokens. To curb this, the team added a task priority queue and a critic model that scores whether each subtask actually advances the goal. Early tests show the new setup triples task completion rates and reduces token usage by 40 %. These results illustrate a practical way to scale autonomous agents without relying on complex planning algorithms.

cases.summary_text: Meta unveiled Llama 5, a 400 billion‑parameter mixture‑of‑experts model that activates 40 billion parameters at a time. It scores 91.2 % on the MMLU benchmark, matching GPT‑4o. Model weights are hosted on Hugging Face under the license, and deploying the full model requires a minimum of eight NVIDIA H100 GPUs.
